analysis:
Examined the three modified provider-swift files: ToolChoicePromptPolicy.swift (head 15-16, 32-34), ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift (head 54-58, 84-90, 165-171) and ToolConstraintSchema.swift (patch hunks adding requireExplicitResponseTypes). No concrete security regression identified.

ToolChoicePromptPolicy: adds glmResponseFormat to Prepared and resolves it via GLM5NextResponseFormat.resolve for every request. Resolve is expected to return nil for non-GLM model types; its implementation is outside the supplied evidence. The Flint path is unchanged: when a Flint responseFormat exists it still overrides the choice, and prepared.glmResponseFormat is carried through only on the non-tools branch (the tools branch builds a fresh Prepared that drops it). That is harmless because the GLM and Flint model types are exclusive.

ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy: GLM models now use .structuredPostValidation (prompt-forced, withheld, schema-validated) instead of throwing as unsupported. validateParser fails closed unless the format is .glm5. advertisesCapability requires both the GLM modelType and a managed model ID (isManagedModelID), so a caller-supplied label alone cannot advertise. forcedStrategy keys only on modelType, which is consistent with the existing mimo_v2 pattern. Whether the GLM engine actually withholds output until validation (analogous to T-008/A-001 fail-closed handling) is not visible here. The claim that media refuses forced choice before any media work rests on code outside this diff.

ToolConstraintSchema: requireExplicitResponseTypes tightens response_format schema acceptance by rejecting untyped nodes. This is stricter, and recursion is bounded by the earlier compile depth check. It does not recurse into anyOf/oneOf/allOf, but compileSchema's handling of those is unseen. It is a correctness/availability tradeoff rather than a security issue.

No changes touch the coordinator trust boundary, keys, attestation, or cache. Open integration questions: GLM5NextResponseFormat, GLM5NextPromptPolicy and GLM5NextCoordinatorServing implementations, and the GLM output-withholding path, were not supplied.
